title: Tight Puncturing-Correlation Bound for Modular Addition
summary: A general puncturing-correlation lower bound for modular addition can be loose; derive an always-tight bound that exploits the output mask’s form.

formal_statement.body: For bit puncturing applied to modular addition, a general lower bound on the retained Walsh-spectrum mass, equivalently the puncturing correlation, is not always tight because it does not fully account for the form of the output mask $w$. The unresolved task is to derive a lower bound on this puncturing correlation that uses the form of $w$ in more detail and is always tight. The existing bound is tight when the case $\sigma_{l-1}=0$ never occurs, a condition that holds for some $w$; the desired result should therefore also handle the dependence on this condition and on $w$.

scope.domain: Walsh-spectrum and linear-correlation analysis of bit-punctured modular addition.
parameters: Output mask w, whose form affects the tightness of the lower bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive an always-tight lower bound that uses the form of the output mask and accounts for the condition involving sigma at index l minus 1.

citations.label: Improved Cryptanalysis of ChaCha: Beating PNBs with Bit Puncturing

progress.summary: The source gives a general lower bound and notes that it is tight for some output masks when the stated sigma-zero case never occurs. It explicitly leaves an always-tight, mask-sensitive bound as an open problem.
citation_labels: Antonio Florez-Gutierrez et al., Improved Cryptanalysis of ChaCha: Beating PNBs with Bit Puncturing
